negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-registered core banking software product vendor was found. All core banking in ME appears to be supplied by foreign/regional vendors, with ME firms acting as integrators, front-end/CRM suppliers or channel operators.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the vendor-intelligence signal for core banking in ME must be harvested from bank-side disclosures and regional vendor sites (workstreams other than A6), not from ME corporate reference pages.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-based card production or card personalisation bureau identified.

negative_findings.result_summary: 'Izlagači' returns fair/trade-show usage; ME banking events publish 'sponzori' and 'partneri' pages but generally not an 'izlagači' page, because these are conference-format not expo-format events.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection queries and page-path heuristics should target /sponzori/, /partneri/, /sponsors/, /partners/ rather than exhibitor paths; assuming an exhibitor list exists will produce false 'missing page' signals.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin media article naming a specific core-banking or payments vendor under contract with a named Montenegrin bank was surfaced, despite targeted sr queries combining bank names with Asseco/ASEE, Halcom, and generic 'dobavljač'/'tehnološki partner' phrasing.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries returned infrastructure-level coverage (SEPA, TIPS Clone, FinTech Strategy 2025-2029) and institutional actors (CBCG, Bank of Italy, World Bank, EPC), but no article-level bank-to-vendor contract attribution.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor attribution in ME appears to live inside interviews, conference coverage and vendor-side press rather than in news headlines — so the collection design must prioritise Bankar.me interviews and event write-ups over generic news crawling, and must be paired with vendor-side and tender sources from other cells.

negative_findings.description: Neither vijesti.me nor a separate 'Bankar Magazin' print edition was confirmed by an actually-retrieved page in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vijesti appears only as a Wikipedia entry in the result sets; 'Bankar Magazin' as a distinct print product separate from the bankar.me portal was not evidenced. Bankar.me itself is well confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two named cell targets remain unverified. Vijesti is likely the single highest-value general outlet for contract reporting, so failing to confirm its section structure leaves a real gap; the print magazine, if it exists, may carry CIO interviews never posted online.

negative_findings.description: Direct automated fetch of the Bankar.me Montenegro-banking category returned HTTP 403.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 Forbidden on WebFetch; the same domain's article URLs appear consistently and recently in search indexes, so the site is live and bot-defended rather than down.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most valuable source in this cell will need a headless-browser or header-spoofing collector, or an RSS path, and must not be marked dead by a naive liveness check.

negative_findings.description: Local IT vendors serving Montenegrin banks were only partially mapped; Logate (Podgorica IT company, organiser of the Infintech conference) surfaced, but the wider domestic supplier set was not enumerated.
negative_findings.result_summary: One domestic vendor identified via conference coverage; search budget was exhausted before a dedicated vendor-side sweep could run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Domestic integrators are frequently the actual implementers behind bank platform stories in small markets; without their inventory, media mentions cannot be resolved to suppliers.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search budget (200/200) was exhausted mid-cell, cutting off planned sweeps of Logate/Infintech vendor coverage, RTCG/antenam/aktuelno banking sections, and Standard (standard.co.me).
negative_findings.result_summary: Last two planned sr queries were refused by the search tool.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cell coverage is good but not exhaustive; a follow-up run with fresh budget should complete the vendor-side and second-tier-outlet sweeps.

negative_findings.description: Halcom's publicly published customer bank list (fetched) enumerates Slovenia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Albania, but contains no Montenegro section or Montenegrin bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: No ME entry found on the vendor's own customer list at the time of this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests Halcom has no (or unpublished) Montenegrin bank footprint — a whitespace signal, and a reminder that some regional vendors genuinely skip ME rather than serving it quietly.

negative_findings.description: Searches in both Serbian and English for a named regional-integrator case study describing a specific Montenegrin bank project (core banking, cards, channels) returned only generic claims (e.g. ASEE stating Basel/IFRS9 implementations across a country list including Montenegro) — no discrete, citable ME reference page was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Country-list-level claims only; no per-project ME case study surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell hypothesis that ME references are aggregated into regional country lists rather than published as standalone references — collection must therefore parse country lists and app metadata, not hunt for case-study pages.

negative_findings.description: No evidence found linking Bosnian integrators Lanaco, Prointer or M&I Systems (and their BiH peers) to Montenegrin bank projects, in either language.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned no BiH-vendor-to-ME-bank connections.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Sarajevo/Banja Luka spillover leg of this cell is currently unevidenced; either the channel does not exist or these vendors publish nothing. Needs a dedicated pass on BiH vendor sites and BiH tech media before concluding.

negative_findings.description: The term 'Adriatic' is heavily polluted: Adriatic Bank AD Podgorica (a Montenegrin bank) dominates English-language results for 'Adriatic ... Montenegro bank', crowding out genuine Adriatic-region vendor content. Similarly 'Crna Gora' collides with 'Razvojna banka Crne Gore' and 'Centralna banka Crne Gore' regulatory documents.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query noise identified; English 'Adriatic region vendor' queries produced almost no vendor-side results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Future query design must pair 'Adria/Adriatic/regionalni' with vendor-side terms (integrator, implementacija, reference, isporučilac, rješenje) and negative-filter the bank name.

negative_findings.description: Run languages were limited to sr and en; Croatian-specific phrasing (rješenje/rješenja vs rešenje, 'referentna lista', 'implementacija u banci') was only partially exercised, and no dedicated hr-language query set was run against Croatian vendor sites (Combis, King ICT, Span, Multicom, Infobip).
negative_findings.result_summary: Croatian-language coverage incomplete by design of the run scope.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Zagreb is one of the three cities from which ME is served; missing hr-language coverage likely under-counts Croatian vendors' ME references.

negative_findings.description: Targeted local-language query combining Montenegrin job-ad terms with named core-banking products ("Crna Gora" banka posao "Asseco" OR "Oracle Flexcube" OR "Pexim" OR "Temenos" iskustvo oglas) returned only generic vendor encyclopaedia pages and non-ME job ads.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Montenegrin job advertisement naming a specific core-banking platform was surfaced through general web search this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's central hypothesis — that ME bank job ads name their core platform — is untested. It likely requires site-internal search of zzzcg.me/srm and bank ATS pages rather than general web search, since those bodies are poorly indexed.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn company pages and vendor posts tagging Montenegrin clients could not be inspected; the platform is auth-walled and its terms prohibit automated collection.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the CKB Bank company-page URL was recoverable; no post content read.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor-tags-client LinkedIn posts are one of the two named pillars of this cell. Without a manual analyst seat or a licensed provider, this channel stays effectively closed.

negative_findings.description: The Administrative Court (Upravni sud Crne Gore) appeal layer above procurement-commission decisions, and the central e-procurement system (CEJN / ESJN) contract-award records, were queued but not searched — the session's web-search budget was exhausted (200/200 calls) before those queries ran.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two planned local-language queries were not executed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Upravni sud rulings and CEJN award notices are the two remaining high-yield public windows into contested and awarded ME banking/IT tenders; the appeals database alone gives only the first instance.

negative_findings.description: No GitHub organisation, public repository, or technology-stack fingerprint source specific to Montenegrin banks or their local integrators was identified. No local-language term exists for this channel; the search vocabulary is inherently English/technical.
negative_findings.result_summary: GitHub / tech-stack fingerprinting sub-channel of the cell remains unpopulated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Mandatory local-language coverage is not achievable for this sub-channel, and it was not covered in English either — a real hole in the cell.

negative_findings.description: The CKB careers ATS page returned only its client-side shell on fetch; department filters including 'IT i operacije' were visible but no job bodies.
negative_findings.result_summary: Source confirmed to exist and to be structured usefully, but content not readable without JS rendering.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Signals that bank-side ATS pages across ME will generally need a headless browser or the ATS vendor's public JSON API, which changes the collection design for this whole source family.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific EY 'Banking Barometer' or SEE banking barometer edition was located. EY Banking Barometer editions found are Switzerland/Liechtenstein; the EY-IIF risk survey is global.
negative_findings.result_summary: Seed-query assumption of an 'EY/Deloitte SEE banking barometer' covering ME is not confirmed; regional coverage appears to run through Deloitte CE/CEE surveys and EY Adriatic content instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids a false expectation of a recurring ME-specific benchmark study; collection should instead target regional CEE surveys and grep for Montenegro mentions.

negative_findings.description: No KPMG Montenegro legal entity appeared in the ICAM register of 37 licensed audit firms returned, and no ME-locale KPMG site was confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Of the Big-4, Deloitte DOO, Ernst & Young Montenegro DOO and PricewaterhouseCoopers DOO are confirmed on the Montenegrin audit-firm register; KPMG was not observed there.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Changes the adviser actor map: statutory bank audits in ME are likely split among three Big-4 firms plus mid-tier (BDO, Crowe MNE, HLB Mont Audit, TPA), which narrows who to monitor.

negative_findings.description: Planned queries on EBRD Montenegro financial-sector diagnostics and on rating-agency (Moody's/S&P/Fitch) reports on Montenegrin banks could not be run.
negative_findings.result_summary: WebSearch session budget (200/200) was exhausted after four queries in this slice; EBRD and rating-agency candidates are therefore inferred rather than observed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Two named components of the cell brief (EBRD assessments, credit-rating bank reports) are under-evidenced and must be re-scouted in a follow-up run.

negative_findings.description: No publicly indexed Montenegrin bank external-auditor report explicitly describing an 'informacioni sistem' / IT-controls review was surfaced; the sr query returned the statutory framework and the CBCG repository instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: IT-controls findings, if published at all, are embedded inside the audited financial statements PDFs on cbcg.me and individual bank sites rather than as standalone documents.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be full-text PDF parsing of bank annual reports, not URL-pattern discovery of separate IT-audit reports.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search quota (200/200) was consumed before the cell's later query lines could be run, specifically the Uprava za digitalizaciju i informacionu bezbjednost / implementer queries and the English 'Montenegro e-government payment implementer' query.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only 4 of the planned ~12 queries executed (3 sr, 1 mixed). Coverage of the state-digital-counterpart half of the cell is therefore shallower than the archive half.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The implementers named in digital-agenda execution records are the highest-value output of this cell and remain largely unenumerated.

negative_findings.description: Fetched https://www.gov.me/clanak/sistem-za-elektronsko-placanje in full; it names the system (NS NAT) and the owning ministry but discloses no vendor, integrator, acquirer bank, funding source or dates.
negative_findings.result_summary: State e-payment implementer not identified from the government's own description page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise: the implementer must be recovered from procurement records, gazette decisions or archived vendor case studies rather than from the counterpart's public page.

negative_findings.description: The Strategija digitalne transformacije 2022–2026 PDF (2.2MB, ntpark.me mirror) downloaded successfully but remote text conversion returned unusable output; institutions, budgets and system lists could not be extracted in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Key strategy document acquired but unparsed. This is an extraction problem, not a dead source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: That document is the single richest listing of planned state information systems and e-payment workstreams for this cell.

negative_findings.description: The sr query aimed at archived Montenegrin vendor/bank reference pages returned only live institutional pages and a browser extension listing — no specific archived case-study URLs. General web search does not index Wayback snapshot URLs well.
negative_findings.result_summary: Archived vendor case studies must be reached through the CDX API against a pre-built actor/domain list, not through search engines.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets the collection design: build the actor map first (CBCG bank register + CRPS + tender awards), then archive-enumerate each domain.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin national web-archiving programme (an equivalent of a legal-deposit web archive at the Nacionalna biblioteka Crne Gore 'Đurđe Crnojević' or Državni arhiv Crne Gore) was located in this pass; local terms 'nacionalna biblioteka', 'državni arhiv', 'obavezni primjerak' were not searched due to the budget cut-off.
negative_findings.result_summary: Unverified whether a domestic .me web archive exists as an alternative to Wayback.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If one exists it would hold captures Wayback missed for small local vendor sites; if not, Wayback is a single point of failure for this cell.

negative_findings.description: sluzbenilist.me exposes issue-level registry pages via opaque GUID URLs; whether a full-text search endpoint over all issues exists was not established.
negative_findings.result_summary: Systematic keyword retrieval across the gazette is not yet proven feasible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without full-text search, gazette monitoring degrades to per-issue enumeration, which is far costlier.

negative_findings.description: Repeated sr-language searching for 'novosti' / 'obavještenja' / 'saopštenja' scoped to Zapad banka, Universal Capital Bank and Lovćen banka returned no indexed news-section URL for any of the three. Only corporate/about pages and third-party directory profiles surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: No newsroom URL confirmed for 3 of the 10 banks in this cell. Their websites may carry an unindexed news path, or they may genuinely publish only via social channels.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If the smaller banks have no newsroom, the entire disclosure burden for them shifts to social feeds and vendor case studies — which changes the collection design from crawling to analyst-assisted monitoring.

negative_findings.description: Across every query in both languages, not one Montenegrin bank press release was found that explicitly names its core-banking, card-processing or channel technology supplier in prose. The Adriatic Bank Apple Pay launch, the most prominent 2025 ME retail-payments announcement located, was reported without any implementation-partner attribution.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero prose-level vendor attributions from the buyer side; all supplier attribution obtained in this pass came from indirect artifacts (app package ids, vendor case studies, shared service-centre sites).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms and sharpens the cell rationale: the buyer side is a first-class channel for detecting THAT something was bought and WHEN, but almost never WHO supplied it. Vendor-side and technical-artifact sources must carry the attribution.

negative_findings.description: Three fetch attempts failed in this pass: https://www.ckb.me/ (TLS 'unable to verify the first certificate'), https://www.hipotekarnabanka.com/obavjestenja/ (404 on the bare section index), and https://www.nlb.me/novosti (404 on a guessed path).
negative_findings.result_summary: All three are hypotheses about the fetcher or the URL guess, not verdicts about the sites. CKB and Hipotekarna both have indexed live content under those same domains/paths.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A downstream liveness pass must not mark these dead. CKB needs a fetcher with a complete CA bundle; Hipotekarna needs item-level URLs rather than the section index; NLB's news path must be discovered from site navigation rather than guessed.

negative_findings.description: The Hipotekarna Banka on-site search endpoint (https://hipotekarnabanka.com/pretraga/?q=...) reflects arbitrary query strings into indexed pages, and an indexed result was found containing unrelated injected Korean-language spam text rather than bank content.
negative_findings.result_summary: The bank's own search endpoint has been abused for SEO spam injection.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector crawling that endpoint will ingest attacker-controlled text under a trusted bank domain. Content retrieved from /pretraga/ must be treated as untrusted data and excluded from vendor-mention extraction; only canonical /obavjestenja/ item pages should feed the pipeline.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin/Serbian-language equivalent term was found in use by the banks for supplier-facing concepts such as 'technology partner' or 'implementation partner'. Bank communications use generic terms ('rješenje', 'novi sistem', 'u saradnji sa') rather than any consistent procurement vocabulary.
negative_findings.result_summary: There is no reliable sr-language keyword that isolates vendor-disclosure content; keyword-only filtering will under-recall.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must not rely on sr keyword matching for vendor detection. Full-text ingestion plus named-entity recognition against a maintained vendor gazetteer (Asseco/ASEE, Logate, Fleka, Halcom, ProvisionPay, Bankart, e-mon) is required instead.

negative_findings.description: Several cell terms are heavily polluted in search. 'Novosti' collides with the Serbian newspapers Novosti a.d. and Večernje novosti and the Croatian weekly Novosti; 'Vijesti' collides with the major Montenegrin daily Vijesti; 'Nova Banka' collides with the Bosnian bank of the same name (Adriatic Bank's former name); 'Komercijalna banka' collides with Serbian and Bosnian entities; 'Hipotekarna' collides with Banco Hipotecario.
negative_findings.result_summary: Unqualified local-language queries return substantial off-target results, including Wikipedia articles about unrelated media outlets and banks.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: All sr queries in this cell must be domain-scoped or co-constrained with 'Crna Gora'/'Podgorica'/'.me' to be usable; otherwise both search-based discovery and any automated relevance scoring will be badly degraded.

negative_findings.description: Consistent with the cell rationale, no public tender, RFP or contract-award record was located for any commercial bank in Montenegro. The banks are private entities outside the public-procurement regime.
negative_findings.result_summary: No procurement-portal source exists for this cell; only the state-adjacent Central Bank of Montenegro would publish tenders, and that is outside this cell's buyer set.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms there is no shortcut. The collection design must accept that timing and attribution will be reconstructed from launch communications, financial-statement intangibles, app artifacts and vendor self-reporting rather than from any authoritative award record.

negative_findings.description: No public procurement / supplier ('nabavke', 'dobavljači', 'javni pozivi') section could be located for any Montenegrin private bank — CKB, NLB Banka Podgorica, Erste Bank AD Podgorica, Addiko ME, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, Prva banka, UCB, Adriatic, Ziraat — despite site-scoped and entity-scoped searching in Montenegrin.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned corporate/product pages, press releases and property-sale oglasi, but no standing tender page. CKB was observed issuing a 'javni poziv' via Facebook rather than a procurement webpage.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise: private-bank buying in ME is invitation-based and does not leave a standing public trail. Collection must pivot to press oglasi, social channels, group parents and IFI portals rather than bank websites.

negative_findings.description: No NLB Group supplier/vendor portal or 'postani dobavitelj' page was found in Slovenian or English.
negative_findings.result_summary: Slovenian-language querying ('dobavitelji', 'nabave', 'javna naročila') returned NLB's supplier-factoring product and unrelated Croatian public-procurement material; no group sourcing entry point.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Of the three group parents, NLB is the one with no visible external sourcing gateway — meaning NLB Banka Podgorica's vendor selection is the least observable of the group-owned banks and needs a different approach (people, press, references).

negative_findings.description: etenderi.me refused connection and bankar.me returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: etenderi.me: ECONNREFUSED on https; bankar.me: 403 Forbidden. Both appear in search indexes with recent content.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are two of the highest-value local sources in the cell; both need browser-grade collection (headless browser, realistic headers) or a subscription rather than plain HTTP fetching. Neither should be recorded as dead.

negative_findings.description: Commercial global aggregators (TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, MontenegroTenders, TendersOnTime) advertise 'private tenders' coverage for Montenegro, but no instance of a genuine Montenegrin private-bank tender in their indexes was observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Marketing copy asserts private-sector coverage; no verifying example surfaced in search results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Buying a subscription on that promise is a real risk of spend with no incremental coverage of the private-bank route this cell exists to cover.

negative_findings.description: No evidence found that OTP Group's supplier programme or SAP Ariba rollout explicitly extends to, or publishes notices for, CKB Banka Montenegro.
negative_findings.result_summary: The OTP suppliers page describes registration via vendorman@otpbank.hu, a phased Ariba rollout, a Partner Code of Ethics and DORA ICT-security training, but says nothing about subsidiary scope.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Whether CKB buys through Budapest or locally determines the entire collection strategy for Montenegro's largest bank; this is the single highest-value open question in the cell.

negative_findings.description: cejn.gov.me — the canonical source for this cell — is a client-side-rendered SPA. Both https://cejn.gov.me/tenders and a concrete tender page https://cejn.gov.me/tenders/view-tender/103145 returned only the literal token 'CeJN' via plain HTTP fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: No server-side HTML; no API endpoint identified in this pass. This is a rendering barrier, NOT evidence the portal is down — search engines index individual view-tender URLs, so the portal is presumed live and unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The primary hard-evidence source cannot be collected with simple HTTP fetching; the pipeline needs a headless browser or a reverse-engineered JSON API, otherwise collection silently degrades to the third-party mirror.

negative_findings.description: No open, machine-readable bulk dataset or open-data dump of Montenegrin procurement awards (OCDS-style) was found. Unlike Serbia/BiH, ME appears to expose data only through the CeJN UI, and no data.gov.me procurement dataset surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for a ME procurement API/open-data feed returned only portal UIs, commercial aggregators and NGO analyses.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Longitudinal competitor-share analysis for the public slice will require self-built extraction and normalisation rather than dataset ingestion; budget accordingly.

negative_findings.description: No concrete ME award notice specifically for ATMs (bankomati) or bank card/cash-handling infrastructure was surfaced in this discovery pass — only an adjacent transit 'smart POS terminal validator' procurement (Glavni grad Podgorica) and IT/maintenance contracts (SAP Trezor, CBCG printing).
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language queries using 'bankomati', 'POS terminali', 'nabavka' returned the portal and legal framework rather than matching award documents.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Either ME state buyers rarely tender ATM/card hardware (commercial banks buy it privately, outside the procurement regime), or such notices exist only inside the CeJN SPA and are invisible to search engines. Both readings materially change how much of the ME market this cell can actually see; must be resolved by an in-portal keyword search.

negative_findings.description: https://www.nabavke.com/javne-nabavke-tenderi-crna-gora/ (aggregator country landing path) returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch, while deep per-tender URLs under the same prefix are indexed and reachable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Path is a URL-segment prefix rather than a browsable index; recorded as unverified, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Crawler seeding must start from search-engine-discovered deep links or the site's own search UI, not from a guessed listing root.

negative_findings.description: Montenegrin/Serbian coverage was strong across all subqueries; however no Albanian-language (sq) procurement channel was sought or found, despite a significant Albanian-speaking population in ME (Ulcinj, Tuzi, Plav).
negative_findings.result_summary: All local-language searching in this pass was sr/Montenegrin Latin; en used only for IFI sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Municipal-level notices in Albanian-majority municipalities could be missed, though CeJN publication is in Montenegrin so the risk is low.

negative_findings.description: No TED contract notice or award specifically for a Montenegrin banking/core-banking or payment information system funded by IPA surfaced in general web search.
negative_findings.result_summary: General web search returns only TED platform documentation, not ME-specific banking notices; TED's own faceted search or API is required because notice text is not well indexed by general engines.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that TED must be queried through its native search/API rather than via search engines, otherwise ME financial-sector notices will be systematically missed.

negative_findings.description: EBRD Montenegro results were dominated by non-financial-sector assignments (PIU support/mobility consultancy); no EBRD financial-sector systems contract award for ME was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only one concrete ME award found (MC Mobility Consultants GmbH, PIU establishment/training, EUR 225,900, signed 06/05/2025) — transport, not finance.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: EBRD's ME financial-sector activity may run through credit lines to banks (no public procurement) rather than procured systems contracts, so ECEPP should be monitored but weighted lower than World Bank/TED.

negative_findings.description: No KfW-financed financial-sector procurement notice for Montenegro was found; KfW's visible ME footprint in results is energy (HPP Perućica).
negative_findings.result_summary: KfW appears as buyer only for an energy tender; financial cooperation with ME banks does not appear to generate public procurement notices.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-investing collection effort in a low-yield channel; KfW stays as low-priority monitoring.

negative_findings.description: Montenegrin/Serbian-language searching surfaces national procurement vocabulary well but almost never surfaces supranational award notices, because funders publish awards in English only.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr queries using 'javna nabavka', 'ugovor', 'obavještenje', 'platni promet', 'informacioni sistem' returned national portals, aggregators and EU Delegation news, not IFI award records.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language collection for this cell should target beneficiary-side confirmation (ministries, CBCG, press) rather than the award records themselves, which must be collected in English.

negative_findings.description: IFC Disclosure Portal was inferred as a required channel from first principles but no Montenegro financial-institution disclosure page was actually retrieved in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Listed as a candidate with reduced confidence; no example_urls recorded because none were observed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification must confirm the ME/FI filter yields records before this source is promoted.

negative_findings.description: No evidence found of a Montenegro-domiciled, independent (non-bank) card acquirer or domestic card processor operating its own switch; card acceptance appears to run through bank acquiring arms plus regional/foreign gateways.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in sr and en for local akvajering/procesiranje companies returned only bank product pages, regional gateways (Monri, CorvusPay, AllSecure) and Payten's Podgorica entity.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If confirmed, the ME acquiring value chain is bank-owned with outsourced processing — meaning competitive displacement happens at the bank-vendor contract level, not at the PSP level.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific merchant case-study or reference pages were located on any PSP/processor site during this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Payten, Monri and CorvusPay publish regional product content; the only ME-relevant merchant reference surfaced was the Monri–Glovo BiH/ME partnership reported in media, not on a vendor case-study page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Merchant-reference intelligence for ME will have to come from media, integrator sites and gateway fingerprints on merchant checkout pages rather than vendor case libraries.

negative_findings.description: The contents of the CBCG payment-institution and e-money registers (the actual entity lists) were not retrieved in this pass — only the register landing pages were identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: Register index page fetched successfully and four register URLs confirmed; individual register contents not opened.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The actual named entities are the core deliverable of this cell; a follow-up fetch is required before any actor map can be considered complete.

negative_findings.description: AllSecure, Novalnet and directory-listed providers claim or imply Montenegro coverage, but no ME licence, ME bank partnership or ME merchant was confirmed for them.
negative_findings.result_summary: Marketing-page claims only; nothing corroborated against CBCG registers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Treating aggregator/marketing claims as market presence would inflate the perceived competitive set; all such names need register cross-checks.

negative_findings.description: No published merchant discount rate / MDR or acquiring fee schedule was found for ME acquirers in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank POS and e-commerce pages describe the service but were not observed to publish MDR; CKB publishes general terms PDFs which may contain some fee data (unverified).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pricing benchmarking for ME acquiring will likely require tariff PDFs ('tarifnik', 'opšti uslovi') per bank rather than product pages.

negative_findings.description: Searched in both Montenegrin and English for a national card switch / domestic scheme operator in Montenegro (e.g. an equivalent of Serbia's DinaCard or BiH's BH mreža). No such operator was found. The World Bank FSAP technical note instead describes an interoperable ATM/POS network whose routing and settlement occur over the international card scheme networks.
negative_findings.result_summary: No domestic card scheme or national switch operator identified for ME; card routing appears to run entirely on Visa/Mastercard rails, with CBCG's RTGS/DNS as the only interbank infrastructure.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Removes an entire hypothesised actor class from the cell and reframes the vendor question: card-side technology decisions sit with individual banks and their processors, not with a national switch operator, so the leverage point is the CBCG platform plus per-bank processing contracts.

negative_findings.description: Mastercard's Europe newsroom and Visa's public channels were searched in English for Montenegro-specific partnership, launch or certification announcements naming a Montenegrin bank. Nothing Montenegro-specific surfaced in search results; hits were global or other-market items.
negative_findings.result_summary: No ME-specific Visa or Mastercard press announcement found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The scheme-newsroom channel, though conceptually the highest-leverage pointer, appears to be low-yield for a market of Montenegro's size. Collection should treat it as a low-frequency monitor rather than a primary feed, and weight CBCG/UBCG/bank channels higher.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language Visa or Mastercard country page or local newsroom for Montenegro was found. Local-language terms used included 'kartična šema', 'Visa kartice Crna Gora', 'Mastercard Crna Gora'; results returned only bank product pages (Addiko, Erste, Prva banka, CKB), not scheme-operated local channels.
negative_findings.result_summary: Schemes appear to have no ME-localised publishing channel; local scheme-related content lives on issuer bank sites instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means scheme signals for ME must be picked up either from regional/European scheme channels or reconstructed from issuer bank communications and general terms & conditions documents.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Montenegrin for the card-processing supplier behind Montenegrin banks (Payten / Asseco SEE / MultiCard / Chip Card terms). Regional evidence for these vendors exists (Payten as part of Asseco SEE; MultiCard consortium in Serbia), but no result explicitly tied any of them to a Montenegrin bank's processing.
negative_findings.result_summary: Regional processor candidates identified but no confirmed ME engagement in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The bank-by-bank processing vendor map for ME remains open and must be built from bank T&Cs, annual reports, procurement records and vendor reference pages rather than from a single pointer source.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific SWIFT country/user-group source was located in this pass. Searches focused on SEPA and TIPS; a SWIFT national member/user group (NMG) page or ME BIC directory view was not confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: SWIFT-side sourcing for ME is an untested branch, recorded as unverified rather than absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: SWIFT adhesion, ISO 20022 CBPR+ migration and BIC directory data are complementary evidence of which ME institutions connect internationally and which service bureaux serve them.

negative_findings.description: The routine playbook path given in the brief (C:/Users/User/Dropbox/... routine_prompt.md) is a Windows path and is not present on this macOS host, so the full method document could not be read. Work proceeded from the instructions embedded in the brief.
negative_findings.result_summary: Playbook unavailable on this machine.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Some playbook-specific conventions (scoring calibration, subtype taxonomy) may not be exactly matched in this slice.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated CBCG register of card processors / card-acquiring processors or ATM operators was found as a distinct published list. Searches in sr for processing and exchange-office terminology returned only the four payment-side registers plus the bank register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Card processing appears to be covered implicitly, either inside the 'registar platnih sistema' (system operators) or as an authorised service line within the payment-institution register, rather than as a separate list.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cell #9's remit explicitly names card processors; if no discrete register exists, downstream cells cannot derive processor actors from a register and must infer them from payment-system operator entries plus CRPS activity codes.

negative_findings.description: Search for a register of authorised exchange offices ('registar ovlašćenih mjenjača', 'mjenjački poslovi') on cbcg.me returned no such list.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the payment registers and generic financial-system pages were returned; no exchange-office register surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Exchange offices are a cash-handling channel adjacent to payments; their absence from the enumerable set is a coverage limitation to state explicitly rather than assume away.

negative_findings.description: The guessed English-language CBCG URL https://www.cbcg.me/en/key-functions/payment-system/registers/register-of-payment-institutions-and-their-agents returned HTTP 404.
negative_findings.result_summary: CBCG does not use translated English URL slugs; the English tree reuses the Montenegrin slugs under an /eng/ prefix (confirmed by an observed /eng/kljucne-funkcije/... bank-register URL).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any crawler built on translated English paths will silently miss the entire English mirror. Locale handling must be prefix-swap, not slug translation. This is a URL-construction failure, not evidence the English register is missing.

negative_findings.description: The IRMS tax-portal business-entity register search rendered no content to a plain HTTP fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the 'IRMS Portal' shell was returned; the register UI is client-side rendered.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recorded as unverified/hypothesis, not dead. It likely has an underlying JSON API that would be the best structured collection route for ME company data — worth a headless-browser investigation.

negative_findings.description: For both the Capital Market Authority (scmn.me) and the Insurance Supervision Agency (ano.me), the existence of a licence register was confirmed in their own descriptive material, but the direct public register URL was not established in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Regulator homepages and rules pages located; register deep-links not located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These two supervisors cover investment firms and insurers, adjacent buyer segments. Leaving them at homepage granularity weakens the completeness claim of the licensed-actor index.

negative_findings.description: No public structured member directory ('imenik članova') was located for Privredna komora Crne Gore despite a targeted sr-language search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only institutional pages (about, boards, contact) surfaced; no searchable member database.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The chamber would otherwise be the natural industry-side cross-check on the ICT vendor population; without it, vendor enumeration depends more heavily on CRPS activity codes.

negative_findings.description: data.gov.me was confirmed to exist as a national open-data portal, but no specific CRPS, CBCG-register or licensed-institution dataset was confirmed to be published there in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portal and a 'uprava' dataset group were located; the presence of a machine-readable company or licence register dataset remains unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If such a dataset exists it would replace fragile HTML/PDF scraping with a legal, structured feed. Its absence would mean all register collection must be scrape-based.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Montenegrin fintech or payments-industry association was found in either sr or en searching ('fintech asocijacija', 'udruženje', 'payments association').
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only the PKCG banking/finance board, UBCG, and a newly formed CFO association; no fintech/payments trade body exists or is publicly visible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Payments-vendor intelligence in ME must be reconstructed from the bank association, the chamber's finance board and the ICT cluster rather than from a single industry body.

negative_findings.description: Two navigation URLs surfaced by search returned HTTP 404 on fetch: https://komora.me/en/cem/udruzenja-2 and https://www.amcham.me/members/.
negative_findings.result_summary: 404 on both; working equivalents appear to be https://komora.me/en/cem/udruzenja and https://www.amcham.me/en/member-list (the latter taken from the live amcham.me homepage navigation, not yet fetched).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Both sites have recently been restructured; any stored crawl paths for chamber/AmCham directories will need re-derivation rather than being treated as dead sources.

negative_findings.description: Unija poslodavaca Crne Gore (UPCG) and Montenegro Business Alliance do not publish an itemised member-company list on the open web.
negative_findings.result_summary: UPCG publishes board composition and membership categories only; MBA's claimed 500+ members appear only as an aggregate figure in third-party profiles.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Buyer-side mapping from employer bodies will require event attendee lists, board rosters and press rather than a directory scrape.

negative_findings.description: No full German AHK (Delegacija njemačke privrede) chamber exists for Montenegro; searching in sr and de-adjacent terms only returned AHK Croatia/Bosnia.
negative_findings.result_summary: The German business presence is the German-Montenegrin Business Club (njemackiposlovniklub.me) plus the German embassy's economic pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Expectations of an AHK-grade member directory and market reports for ME should be reset; the club is smaller and less document-productive.

negative_findings.description: No publicly posted committee/board minutes (zapisnici sa sjednica odbora) were located for either the PKCG banking board or the PKCG ICT board.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only board composition, secretary contacts and news write-ups of sessions are public; minutes appear to be internal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed minutes would surface vendor presentations; in ME that intelligence must instead be recovered from Glasnik write-ups and news items, or requested from board secretaries.

coverage_gaps.description: Field-service and hardware-maintenance firms (ATM cash-handling, safes, CIT, terminal repair) in ME beyond Payten are essentially invisible in web search.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search sr terms 'servisiranje bankomata', 'transport novca', 'trezorska oprema', 'CIT Crna Gora' and cross-check bank annual reports and CRPS activity codes for outsourced-service suppliers.

coverage_gaps.description: No ME public-procurement channel was mined this run, yet state banks/institutions publish tenders naming winning IT vendors and contract values.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the Montenegro e-procurement portal (CEJN / cejn.gov.me) and the Ministry of Finance tender archive as pointer sources and filter on ICT and payment-system CPV categories.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin Cyrillic-script and ijekavian spelling variants were only lightly exercised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key queries with Cyrillic forms and ijekavian variants (rjesenja/resenja, bankarski sistem, platni promet, informacioni sistem) to reach sources that latinica queries miss.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor employment and project signals (job ads, LinkedIn project posts, conference sponsor lists) were not systematically harvested, though they often name bank projects before marketing pages do.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ME job boards (posao.me, zaposli.me) and the TechnoBank/regional banking-conference sponsor and speaker lists as recurring pointer sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor reference pages are undated, so wins cannot be time-ordered from the page alone.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair each vendor crawl with Wayback Machine snapshots to date the first appearance of each named bank reference.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor partner-locator and 'find a partner' tools were not interrogated directly — they are typically JavaScript applications that web search cannot index.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Drive the partner locators of Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Temenos, Oracle, Thales and IDEMIA with a headless browser, querying country=Montenegro, and capture the underlying JSON endpoints for repeatable collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Card-personalisation and identity vendors (Thales, IDEMIA, Giesecke+Devrient, Veridos) and cash-handling vendors (Glory, CIMA) were not searched against Montenegro in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run vendor+Montenegro and vendor+'Crna Gora' searches for each, plus check CBCG and bank tender archives for card-production and cash-recycler procurements.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side evidence hidden in bank parent-group IT disclosures (NLB, OTP/CKB, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat, Adriatic Bank owners) was not covered — group-level vendor contracts often determine the ME subsidiary's stack.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search parent-group annual reports, IT procurement notices and vendor press releases naming the parent group, then check whether the ME subsidiary is in scope.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor conference and roadshow material (Asseco/Payten SEE user conferences, Mastercard/Visa regional events, Sibos/Money Motion/Fintech Adria agendas) frequently names ME bank clients in speaker bios and session titles, and was not searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Collect agendas and speaker lists from regional payments conferences 2023-2026 and extract ME bank + vendor co-appearances.

coverage_gaps.description: This pass surfaced ME vendor references from 2015 (ASEE/Ziraat) and 2022 (Payten/Hipotekarna) but almost nothing from 2023-2026, so current vendor positions may be stale.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run vendor newsroom crawls with explicit date filtering for 2023 onward, and prioritise the TIPS Clone award notices expected around 2026 as the freshest vendor-attribution event.

coverage_gaps.description: Several vendor newsroom URLs recorded here (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, BPC, Worldline) were inferred as standard newsroom paths and were not fetched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic liveness pass resolve them; where a path 404s, re-discover the newsroom from the vendor homepage rather than dropping the vendor.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical sponsor and speaker rosters for ME events (INFINTECH, IT SPOT, Spark.me, SCMN Montenegro Financial Markets) are not available on the live sites; only the current edition is published.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up an Internet Archive CDX-based backfill for each event domain's sponsor/speaker paths, and add a pre-event 'save page now' step each year so future editions are preserved before the site is overwritten.

coverage_gaps.description: Sponsor tiers on ME event sites are largely logo walls; several sponsor names could not be extracted from text alone.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an image pipeline to the collector: capture sponsor-section screenshots, read alt/src filenames, and OCR the logo wall; store extracted names with a confidence flag.

coverage_gaps.description: The key local trade portal (bankar.me) is bot-defended and social event pages (LinkedIn/Facebook) are login-walled, so two of the richest sponsor/partnership channels are not plain-HTTP collectable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Provision a headless-browser fetch path with realistic headers for bankar.me, and handle social pages via analyst review/screenshot capture rather than automated scraping, to stay inside platform terms.

coverage_gaps.description: No ME-run industry award with a published shortlist was found, so the 'awards' half of this cell is currently served only by foreign awards (The Banker, Global Finance) whose citations rarely name the technology vendor.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair each foreign award win with a search for the winning bank's own press release and LinkedIn post, which typically credits the delivery partner; also monitor Mastercard/Visa regional award programmes for ME country winners.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin/Serbian-language coverage of REGIONAL events (how ME banks appear at Money Motion, BANCEE, Kopaonik-type forums) was not established — regional event sites publish in English/Croatian only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cross-check regional event speaker lists against a maintained roster of ME bank and vendor entity names (CKB, NLB Banka AD Podgorica, Hipotekarna banka, Erste Bank AD Podgorica, Lovćen banka, Adriatic Bank, Universal Capital Bank, Prva banka, Pošta Crne Gore, m:tel, Logate, ICT Cortex members) rather than relying on ME-language search.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-hosted private events (bank roadshows, closed user-group meetings, Visa/Mastercard client days in ME) leave almost no public trace and were not captured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use indirect reveal: LinkedIn posts by bank and vendor employees, hotel/venue event listings in Podgorica and Tivat, and CBCG/UBCG training calendars, to infer these gatherings.

coverage_gaps.description: Vijesti (vijesti.me) — the cell's most prominent named outlet — has no confirmed section URL or article evidence from this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch vijesti.me directly, confirm the economy/business section path and whether an RSS feed or on-site search API exists, and test paywall behaviour on a banking article.

coverage_gaps.description: Standard (standard.co.me) and other second-tier ME dailies/portals were referenced only indirectly (via traffic-analytics pages) and never inspected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest the free Ahrefs competitor lists for pobjeda.me and standard.co.me, then inspect each peer domain's economy section for banking coverage depth.

coverage_gaps.description: Social and video channels of these outlets (Facebook pages for Bankar.me and Portal Analitika, X/@PortalAnalitika, LinkedIn pages for CKB and CBCG) were observed in indexes but not assessed as collection channels.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess LinkedIn company pages of Montenegrin banks as a separate direct source class — in small markets, bank IT go-lives and vendor thank-yous are posted there before any article appears.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival/back-catalogue strategy exists for these outlets; most were assessed only on current front pages and recent articles.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For Bankar.me and eKapija ME, test paginated archive depth and whether historical vendor-deal articles remain reachable; register any that require Wayback fallback.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell mandates sr and en; sr coverage was thorough, but no en-language Montenegrin business outlet (e.g. English editions or expat/business-English portals) was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe whether Vijesti, CdM or eKapija maintain English editions, and whether SeeNews or Emerging Europe carry ME banking-IT items, to give the en side of this cell a real anchor.

coverage_gaps.description: Several ME portals publish syndicated bank PR indistinguishable from editorial (the same 'Partnerstvo koje pokreće uspjeh' item ran on both CdM and sjevercg.me).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build cross-outlet duplicate detection into the collector and flag near-identical multi-site items as PR rather than independent corroboration.

coverage_gaps.description: Bosnian (Sarajevo / Banja Luka) vendor leg of the regional spillover is unmapped: no BiH integrator was evidenced as serving Montenegro.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated pass over BiH vendor sites (Lanaco, Prointer, M&I Systems, Ministry of Programming, Authority Partners, HUB387 members) and BiH tech media, using bs/hr spellings 'rješenje', 'referentna lista', 'banka u Crnoj Gori'.

coverage_gaps.description: No Croatian-language query set was executed against Croatian integrator and fintech sites despite Zagreb being a primary delivery hub for Montenegro.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add hr to the language set for this cell, or at minimum run hr-spelled variants (rješenje, izvještaj, referentna lista, uveden u banci) against combis.hr, king-ict.com, span.eu, multicom.hr, infobip.com.

coverage_gaps.description: No procurement/tender source was captured for Montenegrin banks or state financial institutions; state-owned or state-influenced entities (Razvojna banka Crne Gore, Centralna banka Crne Gore, Pošta Crne Gore) publish tenders naming IT scopes and winning regional bidders.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the Montenegrin public-procurement portal and CBCG/Razvojna banka tender pages as a separate cell/collection target, and cross-reference winners against regional vendor names.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-to-bank attribution exists for only a few of Montenegro's ~11 banks (NLB Banka Podgorica, Adriatic Bank, partially CKB). Hipotekarna, Erste ME, Lovcen, Prva, Universal Capital, Ziraat, Addiko ME, Zapad banka remain unattributed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the app-package-ID attribution method across every ME bank's mobile/e-banking app plus certificate/WHOIS and HTML fingerprints of their e-banking portals to infer the regional supplier.

coverage_gaps.description: Regional bank groups' annual reports and IR decks (NLB, OTP, Intesa, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat) were not mined; these disclose digitalisation programmes and capex rolled down to ME subsidiaries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add group IR/annual-report PDFs as a recurring structured collection target, extracting subsidiary-level technology and channel statements.

coverage_gaps.description: LinkedIn (both ME bank company pages/job posts and vendor posts tagging ME clients) is unreadable under current tooling and terms.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Provision a manual analyst seat with a documented review cadence, or license a compliant social-listening/company-data provider; define a capture template (post URL, date, bank, vendor, product named).

coverage_gaps.description: Second-instance judicial review of procurement appeals (Upravni sud Crne Gore) and the e-procurement award record (CEJN/ESJN portal) were not reached.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run local-language queries: 'Upravni sud Crne Gore presuda javna nabavka žalba', 'elektronski sistem javnih nabavki Crne Gore ugovori', and enumerate the ESJN portal's award-notice search.

coverage_gaps.description: Platform-name evidence inside job ads was never actually observed — only the containers were found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a keyword dictionary (Asseco/ASEE, ASEBA, Temenos T24/Transact, Oracle Flexcube, Pexim/Nova, Hyperion, iCore, Way4, OpenWay, BASE24, ISO 8583, SWIFT, Mastercard/Visa certification) and run it against a full crawl of zzzcg.me/srm archives plus each licensed bank's ATS, then report hit rates before investing further.

coverage_gaps.description: Only CKB, NLB, Prva banka, Erste and Ziraat surfaced; the full licensed-bank list (incl. Hipotekarna, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank, Lovćen banka, Zapad banka, Addiko) plus payment institutions and the card processor layer were not individually swept for job ads or LinkedIn presence.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Take the CBCG list of licensed credit institutions and payment/e-money institutions as the canonical actor map, then run the job-ad and register sweeps entity by entity.

coverage_gaps.description: No developer/tech-stack fingerprinting source (GitHub orgs, ME bank mobile-app SDK teardowns, TLS/HTTP header or app-store metadata fingerprints) was established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Substitute a technical fingerprinting routine for the absent GitHub signal: inspect ME bank mobile apps' store listings and publisher metadata, and passive web-tech fingerprints of e-banking domains.

coverage_gaps.description: Mid-tier and local advisory firms on the ICAM register (BDO, Crowe MNE, HLB Mont Audit, TPA, Baker-Tilly-equivalents, Auditor DOO, Racio-Mont) have not been profiled for banking-sector clients or publications.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the ICAM register, then check each firm's site and the auditor signature blocks in bank annual reports to map who audits which Montenegrin bank.

coverage_gaps.description: EBRD (country strategy, Transition Report, project summary documents, technical-assistance procurement) is unscouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run dedicated EBRD searches and crawl the EBRD project-summary and procurement-notice search filtered to Montenegro / financial institutions.

coverage_gaps.description: Credit-rating agency layer (Moody's, S&P, Fitch, plus regional agencies) for Montenegrin banks and their parent groups is only inferred.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify which ME banks or their parents carry public ratings and set up monitoring of free rating-action press releases and parent-group investor materials.

coverage_gaps.description: The World Bank digital-payments loan is identified only via a press release; project ID, procurement plan and contract awards (STEP) are not yet located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve the project ID on projects.worldbank.org and set standing monitoring on its procurement notices and contract awards - this is the highest-value competitor-identification path in the cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage used sr terms for audit/reporting (revizija, revizorski izvještaj, finansijski iskazi, bankarski sektor) but not for adviser-side marketing vocabulary (digitalna transformacija banaka, konsultantske usluge, due diligence, savjetodavne usluge) or Montenegrin-specific orthography variants.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Second pass with sr queries such as 'digitalna transformacija banaka Crna Gora konsultant', 'savjetodavne usluge bankama Crna Gora', 'dubinska analiza banke Crna Gora' and Cyrillic variants.

coverage_gaps.description: Individual bank annual reports hosted on bank websites (rather than cbcg.me) were not enumerated; several carry richer notes on software capex and outsourcing.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-bank list of investor-relations/financial-report pages (CKB, Hipotekarna, NLB, Erste, Adriatic, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Ziraat, Lovcen) and harvest annual reports directly.

coverage_gaps.description: No enumerated list yet of Montenegrin/regional IT and payment vendors serving ME banks, nor their current and historical domains — the prerequisite input for archive enumeration.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the vendor actor map from CRPS name searches, ujn.gov.me award notices and bank annual-report supplier mentions, then run Wayback CDX per domain against paths matching reference|klijenti|projekti|rjesenja|case|solutions.

coverage_gaps.description: Merged/liquidated Montenegrin banks (the richest archive targets) were not enumerated; only the current CBCG register page was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull historical Wayback snapshots of the CBCG Registar banaka page across 2008-2024 to recover names and domains of banks that no longer exist, then archive-crawl each.

coverage_gaps.description: ujn.gov.me was identified but its award/contract notice listings were not opened, so no ME state IT/payment contract award has actually been read in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Open the notice search on ujn.gov.me (and any CEJN public view), filter for IT/software/payment categories, and archive award PDFs immediately since these listings rotate.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell explicitly names the digital-agenda administration, but the current body responsible for state IT operations (successor to MJUDDM functions, e.g. a Uprava/Direktorat for digitalisation and information security) was not located, so its project and contractor pages are uncovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve the current official name via gov.me organigram, then crawl its projekti / javne nabavke / dokumenta sections and register them as direct sources.

coverage_gaps.description: EU/UNDP/World Bank funded digital projects in ME publish their own tender awards, a channel touched only via one UNDP press release.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add UNDP procurement notices, EU delegation to Montenegro tender pages and TED/EuropeAid award records for ME digital-government lots.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage was met for gazette, strategy and payment terms, but no sr searches were run for archive-specific vocabulary ('arhivirana stranica', 'web arhiva', 'obavezni primjerak', 'Državni arhiv Crne Gore') or for vendor-reference vocabulary ('lista referenci', 'uspješni projekti', 'studija slučaja').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run those sr term sets in a follow-up pass with restored search budget.

coverage_gaps.description: Newsroom/announcement paths remain unmapped for Zapad banka, Universal Capital Bank, Lovćen banka and Ziraat Bank Montenegro. NLB's and CKB's news listing (as opposed to detail) pages are also not yet pinned down.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a shallow full-site crawl of each of the six domains (zapadbanka.me, ucbank.me, lovcenbanka.me, ziraatbank.me, nlb.me, ckb.me) to harvest the sitemap/nav and locate the sr-locale news paths directly, rather than relying on search-engine indexing.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the CKB 2024 audited statements PDF was located concretely. The equivalent annual reports and audited financial statements for the other nine banks were not individually enumerated in this pass, and no multi-year historical series was assembled for any bank.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-bank, per-year annual-report register (10 banks x ~5 years). Source from each bank's own investor/financial-reports page first, with CBCG per-bank balance-sheet pages and SCMN issuer filings as fallbacks for banks that do not publish directly.

coverage_gaps.description: App-store package-id fingerprinting proved to be the single highest-yield vendor-attribution method in this cell, but it was applied opportunistically to only five banks (Prva, Ziraat, NLB, Hipotekarna, Lovćen). CKB, Erste ME, Adriatic, Zapad and Universal Capital were not fingerprinted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Complete the app register for all ten banks across both Google Play and the Apple App Store: capture developer account, package/bundle id, current version, and the full changelog. Then diff quarterly — a package-namespace change is the clearest available signal of a platform re-tender.

coverage_gaps.description: Product terms-and-conditions PDFs ('opšti uslovi poslovanja', 'opšti uslovi za e-banking', card and payment-services terms) were sampled for only two banks (Ziraat, CKB). These documents must name the operator of a service and are therefore a structurally reliable vendor-reveal artifact that this pass barely touched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically harvest every 'opšti uslovi' and 'tarifnik' PDF from all ten bank sites; run entity extraction for processor, scheme and service-centre names (e.g. Bankart, ASEE/e-mon, Asseco, card personalisation bureaus).

coverage_gaps.description: A LinkedIn profile for a Bankart d.o.o. employee surfaced in a query about ME banks' new system implementation, hinting that the Slovenian card-processing house Bankart may serve Montenegrin banks. This was not corroborated by any bank-side or Bankart-side source in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate the card-processing layer specifically: check whether ME banks outsource card issuing/acquiring processing to Bankart or another regional processor, using bank card T&Cs, CBCG payment-system publications and Bankart's own client list. Card processing is a major spend category entirely unmapped in this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: The national instant-payments rollout coordinated by CBCG (with Bank of Italy, ECB and World Bank support) involved these banks and is the largest recent ME payments programme, but no bank-side communication about its technical implementation was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search each bank's own channel specifically for instant-payments launch communications ('instant plaćanja', 'trenutna plaćanja', 'IPS'), and pair with the World Bank project documentation (worldbank.org press release of 2025-07-28 on expanding digital financial services in Montenegro), which as a donor-funded programme may disclose suppliers that the banks will not.

coverage_gaps.description: Two of the highest-signal channels for the smaller banks (LinkedIn and Meta feeds) are login-gated and ToS-restricted against automated collection, yet they are where those banks actually announce launches.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Design an analyst-assisted monitoring routine for roughly 15 social pages (10 banks plus known vendors) rather than attempting automated scraping; alternatively evaluate a licensed social-listening feed covering .me corporate accounts.

coverage_gaps.description: Unknown whether OTP (Budapest) and Erste Group Procurement (Vienna) run sourcing for their Montenegrin subsidiaries centrally, and whether Ariba/EGP events are ever visible externally.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Contact OTP vendorman@otpbank.hu and EGP directly as a prospective supplier; register on SAP Business Network and on the EGP supplier site; record which Montenegrin categories appear.

coverage_gaps.description: Print and online classified/oglasi channels (Pobjeda, Vijesti, Dan) where Montenegrin banks place statutory and commercial notices were not searched in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated sweep of the oglasi/mali oglasi sections of the main Montenegrin dailies and their online notice archives.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank social-media channels were only incidentally covered, yet a CKB 'javni poziv' was found on Facebook rather than the website.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add monitored Facebook/LinkedIn pages for all Montenegrin banks with keyword rules on 'javni poziv', 'poziv za dostavljanje ponuda', 'tender'.

coverage_gaps.description: etenderi.me — the most promising ME-native aggregator with competitor-win analytics and an OCR'd archive of State Commission decisions — could not be inspected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Reach it via headless browser or plain http, evaluate whether its coverage extends beyond obligated buyers, and price the subscription.

coverage_gaps.description: Procurement-appeal jurisprudence (Komisija za kontrolu postupka javnih nabavki decisions) was identified only indirectly via etenderi.me's archive; the primary body's own decision database was not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and add the State Commission's own decision publication endpoint — appeal rulings name losing and winning vendors and reveal technical specifications.

coverage_gaps.description: Other IFI/donor procurement routes touching Montenegrin banks (IFC, World Bank, EIB, EU IPA) were not searched; only EBRD/ECEPP was covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Sweep IFC, World Bank, EIB and EU IPA notice systems for Montenegro financial-sector contracts.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run tr-language queries on Ziraat Bankası satın alma/tedarikçi portal and sl-language queries on NLB nabavne službe.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Track P509405 procurement plan in STEP and CBCG announcements quarterly; the systems-integration and connectivity packages are the commercially relevant ones.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the ME public procurement portal (CJN/e-nabavke) and CBCG procurement notices, filtered on POS, terminal, procesiranje, platni sistem.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the Montenegrin central business register (CRPS / poreska uprava registar privrednih subjekata) to resolve legal entities, ownership and financial filings.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compile a list of top .me e-commerce sites and inspect checkout redirect domains / JS to attribute gateway market share empirically.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Work outward from the CBCG payment-institution register entity list and fetch each named entity's own site.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat key queries in Cyrillic transliteration and in Albanian (pagesa me kartë, terminal POS, Mali i Zi) to catch missed local actors.

Their own newsrooms, general terms & conditions for cards and payment services, and annual reports frequently name the card processor, switch, gateway and 3-D Secure provider.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the 11 banks from the CBCG credit-institution register, then crawl each bank's press section plus its 'Opšti uslovi poslovanja' PDFs for named technology providers and scheme certifications.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mine CBCG 'Tenderi i oglasi' and nabavke.com award documents historically; also check CBCG annual reports and IMF/World Bank technical notes for platform naming.

coverage_gaps.description: SWIFT-side sources (national member/user group, BIC directory, service bureaux serving ME) were not covered in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated pass on swift.com country/community pages, ISO 20022 migration communications, and any ME service-bureau providers.

coverage_gaps.description: The Central Depository Agency (CDA/CDA Montenegro) — the national CSD identified in the World Bank FSAP note — was not scouted, nor were securities settlement links to the payment system.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the CDA's official site, its rulebook and its procurement to the source set; securities post-trade is an adjacent infrastructure-vendor market.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a paginated harvester over the saopstenja listing and back-fill via web.archive.org for years where the CMS has dropped items.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download the 'Pregled registra' PDF from the payment-systems register and manually classify each operator; then run CRPS activity-code sweeps for J62/J63 and K66 to catch processors registered as IT firms.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish which endpoint the authority treats as canonical and pin collection to it; monitor crps.me notice pages for a migration announcement.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a site-scoped crawl of scmn.me and ano.me for 'registar' / 'licence' / 'dozvole' paths and add the concrete register URLs.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Obtain the MONSTAT KD 2010 classification, fix the target code set (K64/K66 financial services and auxiliary activities, J62/J63 IT services), then run CRPS searches by code.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the CBCG URL inventory from https://www.cbcg.me/r/mapa-sajta rather than by hand, and deduplicate entities across locale variants before diffing.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test an anonymous lookup on eFirma; if gated, document the legal access route rather than treating ownership data as unavailable.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch https://www.amcham.me/en/member-list and /en/publications in the verification pass and correct the paths if the site uses a different scheme.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted sr+en queries for 'italijansko-crnogorska privredna komora', 'Turkish business council Montenegro', 'British-Montenegrin', 'Chinese chamber Montenegro' and register any member directories found.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout for a standalone Montenegrin insurers' association and for microcredit/payment-institution groupings, which are distinct buyers of payment and core systems.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Register the LinkedIn company pages of UBCG, PKCG, AmCham ME, ICT Cortex and AMM as monitored channels, and subscribe to any public newsletter sign-up forms.
